summary.intent: Deploy v0.25.0 to staging, then fix a broken Docker API build and investigate/fix slow IPNS publishes and broken token refresh on staging.
summary.outcome: Fixed Docker API build (PR #308), consolidated the web app from dual orval-generated clients to a single shared api-client package (PR #309), fixed IPNS publish latency by making DHT propagation fire-and-forget, fixed token refresh by adding 401 interceptor to the shared api-client, and eventually unblocked release-please to create a v0.25.2 release after extensive troubleshooting of the release tagging pipeline.

repo: The API is a zero-knowledge server that never handles plaintext — it stores opaque blobs and proxies IPFS, which is why it has no workspace package dependencies.

The web app had two separate orval code generations: one in packages/api-client (axios, for SDK/desktop consumers) and one in apps/web/src/api/ (react-query, for the web app) — the react-query hooks were almost entirely unused, with raw function calls used instead.

release-please uses the 'autorelease: pending' label (not just PR title) to track untagged release PRs — manually creating tags without letting release-please do it leaves the label unflipped and causes subsequent runs to abort.

release-please scans ALL merged PRs in repo history for autorelease labels/title patterns — old single-package PRs titled 'chore: release main' collided with the new multi-package title pattern after migration.
The Tag Staging Release action requires running from the release tag commit, so hotfixes must be tagged before re-running it.
packages/crypto was incorrectly listed in release-please extra-files, causing spurious version bumps when crypto had no changes.
The someguy sidecar DHT propagation was being awaited synchronously in IpnsService.publishRecord(), causing 30s+ publish times.
deploy-staging.yml triggers on tags matching v*-staging*, not release tags — staging deployment is always a separate manual step via the Tag Staging Release action.

code.finding: The delegated routing DHT publish was awaited synchronously; changing to fire-and-forget reduced publish time from 30s+ to near-instant since the DB record is the source of truth.
The shared api-client instance needed withCredentials, a refreshAccessToken callback, and a 401 response interceptor with promise deduplication to prevent concurrent refresh races.
The progress-tracking download path was using raw fetch() instead of the api-client axios instance, bypassing auth interceptors; simplified to use ipfsControllerGet with onDownloadProgress.
The generated API client drift check was diffing all of packages/api-client/ including instance.ts and tests — should only diff openapi.json, src/generated/, and src/models/.

pull-request-title-pattern must be set to 'chore: release v${version}' (no ${component}) because the root package has no explicit component name, causing the default pattern to produce unparseable titles like 'chore: release main'.

workflow: Never create release tags manually unless release-please is fully stuck — manual tags leave 'autorelease: pending' labels unflipped, causing all future release-please runs to abort with 'untagged merged release PRs outstanding'.
When migrating release-please from single-package to multi-package config, old release PRs become permanently unparseable — must rename their titles AND check/flip their autorelease labels.
bootstrap-sha only affects commit scanning, not merged PR scanning — it does not help when old release PRs are the source of the abort.
release-please treats grouped release PRs atomically: if N-1 of N package releases already exist, it will not create the missing one and instead aborts.
chore commits do not trigger release-please version bumps — use fix(scope) for CI/build fixes that need to be included in a release.

friction: release-please troubleshooting consumed the majority of the session across 7+ PRs (#307, #310, #311, #312, #313, #316, #317) due to cascading issues from the single-to-multi-package migration.
The 'autorelease: pending' label mechanism was not documented or anticipated — took multiple failed runs to discover it was the root blocker.
Renaming 58+ old release PR titles via GitHub API was required as a workaround but ultimately didn't help since labels were the actual mechanism.
Grafana Cloud free-tier instance hibernation caused a transient 503 failure during staging deploy, requiring manual re-run.
The stale packages/crypto COPY in the API Dockerfile was a silent leftover that only manifested when the expanded package list added a transitive dependency on @cipherbox/core.
Two separate orval code generation configs (one unused for react-query hooks) created a confusing multi-client architecture that masked where token refresh logic should live.
open_items: React Query cache is not cleared on logout or token refresh failure — CodeRabbit flagged this; noted as pre-existing gap not introduced by PR #309.

The v0.25.2 release cycle worked but required yet another manual tag creation — the title pattern fix (PR #317) needs to be validated end-to-end on the next release cycle to confirm release-please can now fully self-manage.
Token refresh fix for the web app (PR #309) should be smoke-tested on staging — the long batch delete operation that exposed the original 401 issue has not been re-tested.
The IPNS publish fire-and-forget change (PR #308) means DHT propagation errors are now only logged, not surfaced to callers — monitoring/alerting on those log lines should be considered.
packages/crypto is now removed from release-please extra-files but has no independent release-please configuration — its versioning strategy going forward is undefined.
